objectives.title: Read the flag
objectives.prompt: From the s.adeyemi foothold, enumerate Active Directory over LDAP: recover svc-moodle's password from its description attribute, confirm the nested group path (IT-Staff -> Registry-Admins), then read flag.txt from the //dc/registry share that only Registry-Admins may open.
hints: s.adeyemi is a normal domain user (s.adeyemi / Student!2024), and any authenticated user may read most of AD over LDAP. Point your resolver at the DC and bind with a plain simple bind: ldapsearch -x -H ldap://<dc> -D 's.adeyemi@brightwell.lab' -w 'Student!2024' -b 'DC=brightwell,DC=lab' '(objectClass=user)' sAMAccountName description memberOf.

Read the object attributes, not just the names: one service account (svc-moodle, the Moodle LMS sync account) has its own password sitting in its description attribute. Administrators do this far too often.

svc-moodle is not a direct member of the group that unlocks the registry share. Map the group memberships (nxc ldap <dc> -u s.adeyemi -p 'Student!2024' --bloodhound --collection All, or follow memberOf by hand): svc-moodle -> IT-Staff -> Registry-Admins. The registry share is restricted to Registry-Admins, so authenticate as svc-moodle: smbclient //dc/registry -U 'BRIGHTWELL\svc-moodle%<leaked>' -c 'get flag.txt'.

steps.title: Name the technique
steps.prompt: What is the name of the activity where an authenticated user reads Active Directory over LDAP to map users, groups and attributes?

steps.title: Find the leaky account
steps.prompt: Which service account leaks its own password in Active Directory? (username)

steps.title: Name the attribute
steps.prompt: Which object attribute holds the leaked password? (one word)

steps.title: Follow the nested group
steps.prompt: svc-moodle is a direct member of which group that is itself nested inside Registry-Admins? (group name)

steps.title: Name the gated resource
steps.prompt: Which group must you belong to in order to open the share that holds the flag? (group name)
